Isolated inherited lens displacement; skeletal and cardiac abnormalities are each below 30%.
Generalized thyroid hormone resistance; hearing and skeletal involvement lack established frequencies. Thyroid antibodies alone do not establish autoimmune disease.
Hormone-producing tumour arising in the pituitary; no additional organ damage applies commonly across the umbrella.

Isolated progressive sensorineural hearing loss; other MYH14-associated syndromes are separate concepts.
Immune-mediated pustular skin eruption; renal and hepatic injury occur in <30%. Reactive leukocytosis does not establish blood-organ damage.
XP/CS combines photosensitive skin disease and progressive neurodegeneration; damaging ocular disease is common (~30%+); type-F-specific frequencies are sparse.
Distal motor neuron disease; muscle weakness is neurogenic rather than evidence of a primary muscle disorder.
Inherited retinal degeneration with severe visual loss and macular abnormalities; optic nerve findings remain ocular.
Immune-mediated injury of cutaneous blood vessels defines the disease; systemic organ involvement occurs in a minority.
Defining eyelid malformations with frequent lacrimal abnormalities and amblyopia; ovarian endocrine dysfunction occurs in <30%.
Carcinoma arising in breast tissue, which has no axis; metastatic sites are not intrinsic organ labels.
Congenital absence of the pericardium defines a cardiovascular malformation; associated symptoms do not establish other organ damage.
Mitochondrial neurodegeneration; optic atrophy/ophthalmoparesis and myopathy each occur in 30-79%; hepatic failure is often valproate-related and excluded.
Anorectal inflammation, usually infectious or immune-mediated according to the definition; radiation injury is an etiologic minority.
Primary magnesium disturbance with defining generalized seizures and intellectual disability; no evidence establishes direct renal damage.
Systemic measles virus infection; rash and upper-airway symptoms are transient, while pneumonia and encephalitis affect a minority.
Tibial peripheral nerve injury causes sensory loss and weakness; downstream motor deficits do not establish direct muscle disease.
Primary antibody immunodeficiency; recurrent infections do not establish common direct damage to another organ across the umbrella.
Thyroid inflammation defines endocrine involvement; autoimmune and other immune-mediated forms account for most cases across this umbrella.
Inherited hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; hypertrophy and associated electrical abnormalities are confined to the cardiovascular axis.
Trichomonas infection, predominantly genital; urinary or oral involvement is not established in ≥30% across the umbrella.
Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing impairment.
Tumour arising in the adrenal medulla, an endocrine organ; no additional organ damage is common across all subtypes.
